sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Jackson County, KY?
sections.html:
Three offices in McKee share the work. The Property Valuation Administrator values parcels, the Sheriff collects the tax, and the County Clerk keeps the land records. The county's officials page gives the contact details.

  • PVA: P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7634, fax (606) 287-7079. It keeps property records and assesses property for tax.
  • Sheriff: P.O. Box 426, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7121. The county lists tax collection among its duties.
  • County Clerk: P.O. Box 339, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7800. It records deeds and mortgages and handles transfers.

Ask the Sheriff's office which payment methods it takes and what hours it keeps, since the county site lists phone numbers and not a payment portal.

sections.h2: When is Jackson County property tax due?
sections.html:
The Kentucky calendar applies: taxes are due by December 31, with a discount for paying early. Under KRS 134.015, a taxpayer who pays by November 1 gets 2 percent off.

Kentucky regular collection schedule used in Jackson County (source: KRS 134.015)
Payment dateAmount
Through November 1Bill less 2 percent
November 2 to December 31Bill as printed
JanuaryBill plus 5 percent
After January 31Bill plus 10 percent

When bills are mailed late, the Department of Revenue can set an alternative timetable that gives a month for each stage. The sheriff stops collecting on April 15, and the clerk takes over unpaid bills. A buyer who gets no bill should call the Sheriff rather than wait, because a missing bill does not cancel the penalty.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Jackson County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the PVA first and ask for a conference. KRS 133.120 makes that conference a required first step before a formal appeal, and it takes place before or during the inspection period.

If the conference does not settle it, file a written petition with the County Clerk. It must state your reasons, identify the parcel and give your opinion of fair cash value. The filing is due one workday after the inspection period closes, so Jackson County owners should not wait for the bill.

The board of assessment appeals holds a public hearing and fixes the value after hearing evidence. Bring items such as these:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, sales contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Any loan or mortgage papers on the property.

Without that evidence the board can deny the appeal. You still pay tax on the value you claimed while the case is pending.

sections.h2: How much does the homestead exemption save in Jackson County?
sections.html:
The exemption removes $49,100 from the assessment for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. That is a large share of a Jackson County house, where the Census median owner-occupied value is $111,500. A median home would be taxed on $62,400, a cut of about 44 percent of its value.

Eligible owners are 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program, and must live in the home. Apply with the Jackson County PVA, and bring a birth certificate, driver's license or passport as proof of age. Disabled owners generally reapply every year unless they are veterans with a service-connected disability or have been found permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

The exemption applies to the owner's own residence, so a seller who moves should tell the PVA and apply again for the new home.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Jackson County house with taxes still owed?
sections.html:
Any balance has to be settled from your proceeds, because the tax is a personal debt of the owner from the assessment date and a lien on the land for up to 11 years. After April 15 the clerk files the bill as a certificate of delinquency and records the lien.

The Department of Revenue explains the sequence that follows. The County Attorney mails a 30-day notice and then, if needed, a second notice within 60 days. A tax sale cannot happen sooner than 90 days after the transfer, and no later than 135 days, under KRS 134.128. The clerk advertises delinquent bills 30 to 45 days before the sale.

Revenue's worked example shows the cost of waiting. A $1,000 bill becomes a $1,254 certificate when it moves to the clerk, and it reaches $1,659.90 if paid after the June advertisement. Those figures use assumed commissions, so ask the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for the real number.

sections.h2: How are deeds and the transfer tax handled in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the County Clerk in McKee, which also issues vehicle and marriage licenses and keeps wills and notary bonds. The clerk collects the state transfer tax before accepting the deed.

KRS 142.050 sets the tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, charged to the grantor. At the Census median value of $111,500 that is 223 units, so the tax is $111.50. Gifts, divorces between spouses and foreclosure transfers are among the exemptions.

Ask the clerk for the current recording fee before closing, since fee schedules are set by statute and can change.

sections.h2: What is Jackson County, Kentucky, like for a seller?
sections.html:
Jackson County sits where the Cumberland Plateau meets the Bluegrass region, with elevations from about 600 to 1,600 feet. Lawmakers formed it in 1858 from parts of Madison, Estill, Owsley, Clay, Laurel and Rockcastle counties. McKee is the seat, and Annville is the largest community.

About a quarter of the county, some 56,000 acres, lies inside the Daniel Boone National Forest, and the Sheltowee Trace trail starts at McKee. US 421 runs north to Richmond and Berea, and KY 30 links the county to I-75 and the Mountain Parkway. The county has no hospital, so residents drive to Berea, Richmond, London or Manchester.

  • 2025 population estimate: 13,325, up 2.8 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Land area: 345.2 square miles, about 37.5 people per square mile.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.4 percent.
  • Median gross rent: $665.
  • Median household income: $40,000.
  • Mean commute to work: 37.7 minutes.

Water comes from the Jackson County Water Association outside McKee, and Jackson Energy supplies power.

faqs.q: Where is the Jackson County PVA office?
faqs.a: It is in McKee, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7634.

faqs.q: How much is the early payment discount in Jackson County?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent. KRS 134.015 gives that discount to taxpayers who pay in full by November 1, then charges the printed amount until the end of December.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying a Jackson County tax bill late?
faqs.a: The penalty is 5 percent in January and 10 percent after January 31. After April 15 the bill moves to the County Clerk, where interest of 1 percent per month and commissions are added.

faqs.q: Can a Jackson County seller claim the homestead exemption on the old house?
faqs.a: Only while the seller lives there. The exemption applies to the owner's primary residence, so the seller should tell the PVA after closing and apply for the new home separately.

faqs.q: Does Jackson County record deeds at the courthouse in McKee?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Clerk in McKee records deeds and mortgages and collects the 50 cents per $500 transfer tax. Call (606) 287-7800 for fees before you close.
